newsitem.title: JAPAN: THAIS ASKED JAPAN BANKS FOR SUPPORT - JAPAN BANKER.
newsitem.headline: THAIS ASKED JAPAN BANKS FOR SUPPORT - JAPAN BANKER.

text.p: Thailand's finance minister and central bank governor asked Japanese banks on Tuesday to continue their support for the country, an official of a Japanese bank told reporters.

There were no specific requests by the Thai officials for new money or a rolling over of existing loans, but Japanese bankers took the Thai request for continued support to mean that they want existing loans to be rolled over, the banker said.

"The Thai finance minister and central bank governor asked us to continue the support that we have given them in the past," said the senior bank official, who attended the meeting but did not want to be identified.
Thailand also told the bankers it would protect depositors and creditors at 42 Thai financial institutions whose operations were recently suspended, the banker said.
Creditors and depositors would continue to receive interest payments and their deposits and loans would be protected in full, the banker quoted the Thai officials as saying.
"The Thai central bank governor told us that Thailand will be able to restore overall confidence in the financial industry (through these measures)," he said.

Asked whether the Thai officials' explanations had reassured Japanese banks regarding the loans they had extended to Thai financial institutions, the banker said that, if the loans were indeed going to be protected, that would be reassuring.
The banker also said it was up to each individual Japanese bank to decide whether to continue to give Thailand their support.
He added that the Thai finance minister had said he does not want Japanese firms and banks to withdraw from Thailand.

Thai Central Bank Governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi and Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya met representatives of 21 major Japanese commercial banks a day after a multilateral conference in Tokyo agreed to provide $16 billion to help overcome Thailand's financial crisis.
